note: A shrunk counterexample of the fuzz suite's inversions, kept on 2026-10-08 with ves-bessel-tables-578342b9.json. A Schlumberger sounding of about 5 ohm-m with a reading of 7.9 ohm-m at the first spacing, inverted to three layers. The browser built its quadrature tables from Numerical Recipes' J0 and J1, good to 5e-9. Under a thin resistive top layer the forward model is the top layer's resistivity plus an integral that cancels nearly all of it, so that error reached the apparent resistivity multiplied by rho1 / rho_a: 1.5e-4 at 10,000 ohm-m and 1.5e-3 at 100,000 over a few ohm-m (reference.json's ves_forward grid). As the search pushed the top layer's resistivity up the two paths drifted apart, until at iteration 12 the browser's finite-difference step on the top layer's thickness straddled a jump in the quadrature's truncation, which both engines share, and gave it a Jacobian entry of 7.2. The browser then ran along the 200,000 ohm-m bound until its 60 iterations ran out (converged false, a 1.303 percent fit) while Python stopped at 85,788 ohm-m with 1.456. The browser now builds its tables from Cephes j0 and j1, as scipy does, and stops where Python does. Perturbing Python's forward model by 1e-15 to 1e-10 as a cosine in the log of the spacing moves its own answer by at most 1.5e-4; over the four shapes, and readings perturbed as well, at up to 1e-7 every closed VES case moves by at most 1.6e-4, inside parity's 1e-3.
